change_control: Version 3 explicitly defers comparative ABI selection on 12 September 2026. Preserve version 2 and its raw runs. Dedicated-host correctness/progress limits and optional statistical parameters are unchanged.
sequence: implement B and confirm through generated code
reconsider comparative timing only for a demonstrated problem
initial_workload_weights: Equal weights in the retained exploratory run. Census-informed weights are needed only for a future representative comparison; they do not block implementing B.
run_order: Seeded randomized paired candidate/baseline trials on the same dedicated host and engine tier.
estimator: Geometric mean of paired runtime ratios across the fixed workload weights; paired bootstrap over independent trials, not inner iterations, with seed and 10000 resamples recorded.
uniform_rule: Optional future comparison only: choose the simplest candidate whose upper 95% confidence bound for runtime ratio to the measured best is at most 1.05. This rule was not used to choose B; the current choice is engineering judgment.
engine_policy: Pin engine/version/tier, host CPU/OS, flags and toolchain. Qualify multivalue, tail calls, selected EH encoding, shared-memory atomics and bulk memory explicitly. JSPI is required only for its profile. No cross-engine pooling.

dedicated_host_progress_limits.scope: Controlled harness on the recorded dedicated host; these limits do not promise browser background-tab or OS scheduling latency. A timeout fails the run and is investigated, never counted as success.

ratio_definitions: runtime_ratio = candidate runtime / baseline runtime; speedup = (1 / runtime_ratio) - 1. Resource growth = candidate / baseline - 1.
future_enhancements: H(G) is optional future work, with no required experiment or gate at any scheduled stage.
granularity: Production packaging remains a Stage 1 decision. Use B with the chosen packaging; investigate cross-module cost on generated code if it is a demonstrated bottleneck. No packaging or ABI ranking sweep is required before implementation.
selection_basis: 12 September 2026 user direction: choose a simple clear implementation and stop spending effort ranking near-equal exploratory timings. B is the existing simplicity baseline; no statistically demonstrated speed advantage is claimed.
future_comparison_requirements: If comparative timing is reopened, first establish sensitivity at the relevant cost scale, freeze representative weights and engine/granularity assumptions, and collect the required metrics. Do not run that work now.
